claims.text: A compositionally graded Cu–Ni interlayer can be deposited between a Cu substrate and an HEA coating.
The Cu–Ni interlayer should be followed by an optimized post-deposition annealing treatment.
The graded Cu–Ni interlayer gradually transitions the chemical properties between the Cu substrate and the HEA coating.
The graded Cu–Ni interlayer gradually transitions the thermal properties between the Cu substrate and the HEA coating.
A Cu–Ni interlayer enhances chemical compatibility between Cu and the HEA coating.
A Cu–Ni interlayer reduces thermal-expansion mismatch between Cu and the HEA coating.
Annealing promotes interdiffusion across the Cu/Cu–Ni/HEA interface.
Interdiffusion during annealing forms a robust metallurgical bond.
The Cu–Ni interlayer minimizes interfacial defects.
The Cu–Ni interlayer reduces residual stresses at the coating–substrate interface.
HEAs possess inherent wear resistance.
The graded Cu–Ni interlayer will significantly improve metallurgical bonding compared with direct HEA deposition on Cu.
The graded Cu–Ni interlayer will increase HEA-coating adhesion strength and durability on Cu.
The graded Cu–Ni interlayer will improve wear resistance relative to direct HEA deposition on Cu.
The coating system will exhibit improved wear resistance under mechanical and thermal cycling.
An improperly controlled Cu–Ni composition gradient may form brittle intermetallic compounds.
Brittle intermetallic phases formed in the graded layer may compromise coating performance.
The benefits of the interlayer may be reduced if post-deposition annealing parameters are not appropriately tuned.
The optimal Cu–Ni composition gradient is not yet established.
The annealing conditions needed to maximize bonding while avoiding deleterious phases are not yet established.
